jobs: A neighbour asks how someone makes a living and expects to hear the regular paid activity that supports them.
At a party, one guest asks another what they do to earn a living and receives the name of a paid role.
A biography explains how its subject earned their living before becoming famous.
Someone asks what line of paid activity a new acquaintance is in because they want to know how that person supports themselves.
A form asks for the main way a person earns their living rather than their hobbies or family role.
Two strangers discuss what each of them does during the week to support themselves financially.
A parent asks which regular paid activity their adult child relies on to make a living.
The phrase about doing something for a living is used to ask for a person's usual income-producing role.
